name: Auryn
description: Auryn is Lazarus's flagship recreational compound — a multi-pathway hedonic saturator that simultaneously activates opioid, dopaminergic, and serotonergic systems in a carefully tuned cascade that produces what clinical literature describes as 'sustained positive affective saturation.' Users simply feel good — completely, totally, without anxiety, want, or discomfort. It is the most expensive and most dangerous recreational drug that Lazarus sells legally.
effects: Total hedonic saturation — profound, all-encompassing sense of wellbeing
Elimination of all negative affect — no fear, grief, anger, or discomfort
Warm physical euphoria throughout the body
Sense of completeness — nothing is missing, nothing is needed
side_effects: Extreme addiction — single-use dependency reported in clinical literature
Post-dose anhedonia lasting days to weeks
Long-term use rewires baseline hedonic set-point — normal life becomes permanently insufficient
Withdrawal is medically dangerous and requires clinical management
cultural_context: Auryn is the worst-kept secret of the Spire. Tier 5 residents use it as a scheduled indulgence — quarterly, with medical supervision and withdrawal management. The idea of 'an Auryn evening' is a mark of extreme wealth. On the Shelf, a crude analog called 'Bliss' circulates at Φ150 per dose with none of the safety controls — it is destroying communities faster than any other single compound. Lazarus funds anti-Bliss PSA campaigns while quietly lobbying against generic pharmaceutical regulations that would undercut their market.
story_hooks: A Tier 5 Lazarus executive has been on an Auryn cycle for six months without the mandated medical breaks — his family wants someone to intervene, but he controls enough of the company to make that extremely dangerous

The Shelf analog 'Bliss' has begun appearing in Tier 2 neighborhoods at prices lower than Velora — someone is subsidizing the distribution, and the motive for flooding working-class communities with an extreme addiction compound is not humanitarian

A Lazarus whistleblower has evidence that Auryn's addiction profile was known from Phase 1 trials and the company buried it — she needs protection long enough to get the data to someone who can actually use it
